:::{#def-column-space}
#### Column space (range, image)

The **column space** of an $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$ is

$$
\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})
\eqdef
\cb{\matr{A} \vecf{x} : \vecf{x} \in \reals^n},
$$

the set of all vectors $\matr{A} \vecf{x}$ in $\reals^m$.
It is also called the **range** or **image** of $\matr{A}$.
The **row space** of $\matr{A}$ is $\mathcal{C}(\tp{\matr{A}})$,
a set of vectors in $\reals^n$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-column-space}
#### The column space of a rank-one matrix

Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & -6 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

For any $\vecf{x} \in \reals^3$,
$\matr{A} \vecf{x} = (x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3,\; 3\,(x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3))
= (x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3)\,(1, 3)$ (@def-matvec-mult).
The number $x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3$ can be any real number
(take $x_2 = x_3 = 0$),
so $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \cb{c\,(1, 3) : c \in \reals}$,
a line in $\reals^2$.
The vector $(1, 0)$ is not in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$:
$c\,(1, 3)$ has second entry $3c$,
which is $0$ only if $c = 0$, and then the first entry is $0$, not $1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-column-space-span}
#### The column space is the span of the columns

If $\matr{A}$ is an $m \times n$ matrix
with columns $\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_n$, then

$$
\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \operatorname{span}\cb{\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_n},
$$

so $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$ is a subspace of $\reals^m$,
and the row space $\mathcal{C}(\tp{\matr{A}})$ is a subspace of $\reals^n$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-matvec-columns,
$\matr{A} \vecf{x} = x_1 \vecf{a}_1 + \cdots + x_n \vecf{a}_n$,
and as $\vecf{x}$ ranges over $\reals^n$,
the coefficients $\dsn{x}$ range over all lists of $n$ numbers.
So the set of all $\matr{A} \vecf{x}$ (@def-column-space)
is the set of all linear combinations of the columns,
which is their span (@def-span).
A span is a subspace (@thm-span-subspace).
Applying the same argument to $\tp{\matr{A}}$,
whose columns are the rows of $\matr{A}$,
shows the row space is a subspace of $\reals^n$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-column-space-span}
#### Reading off the column space and row space from the columns and rows

For $\matr{A}$ in @exm-column-space,
the columns are $(1, 3)$, $(-2, -6) = -2\,(1, 3)$ and $(-2, -6) = -2\,(1, 3)$,
so by @thm-column-space-span
$\mathcal{C}(\matr{A}) = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 3)}$,
the same line found in @exm-column-space.
The rows are $(1, -2, -2)$ and $(3, -6, -6) = 3\,(1, -2, -2)$,
so the row space is $\operatorname{span}\cb{(1, -2, -2)}$,
a line in $\reals^3$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-null-space}
#### Null space (kernel)

The **null space** of an $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$ is

$$
\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})
\eqdef
\cb{\vecf{x} \in \reals^n : \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m},
$$

the set of [solutions](#def-linear-system) of the linear system $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m$.
It is also called the **kernel** of $\matr{A}$.
The **left null space** of $\matr{A}$ is $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}})$,
a set of vectors in $\reals^m$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-null-space}
#### The null space and left null space of a rank-one matrix

For $\matr{A}$ in @exm-column-space,
$\matr{A} \vecf{x} = (x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3,\; 3\,(x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3))$,
so $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_2$ exactly when $x_1 = 2x_2 + 2x_3$.
Writing $\vecf{x} = (2x_2 + 2x_3, x_2, x_3) = x_2\,(2, 1, 0) + x_3\,(2, 0, 1)$
shows $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A}) = \operatorname{span}\cb{(2, 1, 0), (2, 0, 1)}$,
a plane in $\reals^3$.

For the left null space,
$\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{y} = (y_1 + 3y_2,\; -2\,(y_1 + 3y_2),\; -2\,(y_1 + 3y_2))$,
which is $\vzero_3$ exactly when $y_1 = -3y_2$,
so $\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}}) = \operatorname{span}\cb{(-3, 1)}$,
a line in $\reals^2$.

:::
